confidence.rationale: These indices have different statistical definitions and can vary independently; the included longitudinal meta-analyses explicitly address different forms of change.

limitations: The distinction does not select one personality taxonomy or establish the causes of change.

scope.population: Humans assessed repeatedly with declared personality trait measures.
scope.temporal_scope: Two or more comparable personality assessments.

claims.statement: Personality development must distinguish rank-order continuity, mean-level change, individual differences in change, repeated behavior, and measurement change rather than treating any one index as the whole person.

confidence.rationale: The meta-analysis synthesized many longitudinal samples, but historical measures, cohort differences, attrition, age coverage, and trait categorization limit a universal developmental schedule.

claims.confounding_note: Cohort, period, instrument, attrition, retest interval, sampling, health, roles, and historical context can contribute to observed age-related mean changes.

estimate.metric: meta-analytic standardized mean-level change by trait and age
estimate.notes: Social dominance, conscientiousness, and emotional stability increased especially from ages 20 to 40; social vitality and openness rose in adolescence and declined in old age; agreeableness changed mainly in old age.

limitations: A population average is not a prescription, universal maturation law, or prediction for one person.

boundary_conditions: The six trait categories, age groups, instruments, cohorts, and intervals represented in the 2006 meta-analysis.
scope.population: Participants represented in 92 longitudinal personality samples across adolescence, adulthood, and old age.
scope.temporal_scope: Source-specific longitudinal intervals across the life course.

claims.statement: Across 92 longitudinal samples, average personality trait scores changed across the life course, with especially notable young-adult increases in social dominance, conscientiousness, and emotional stability and different patterns for other traits and ages.

confidence.rationale: The large preregistered synthesis quantified change heterogeneity across 230,492 participants, while estimates still depend on model, measure, interval, age, reliability, and publication coverage.

claims.confounding_note: Reliability, longitudinal invariance, attrition, interval, age, trait breadth, model specification, and sample selection affect estimated change heterogeneity.

estimate.metric: meta-analytic variance in individual personality trait change
estimate.notes: Significant individual differences occurred for all traits, were most pronounced in childhood, remained present across the lifespan, and increased with longer intervals.

limitations: Evidence that people differ in change does not reveal the causal source or allow accurate prediction of one person's trajectory.

boundary_conditions: Individual change variance is interpreted after accounting for measurement error under the included models.
scope.population: 230,492 participants represented in 229 longitudinal studies from childhood through old age.
scope.temporal_scope: Source-specific repeated assessments across the lifespan.

claims.statement: A 2026 meta-analysis of 229 longitudinal studies found reliable individual differences in change for every studied personality trait across the lifespan.

confidence.rationale: Changes replicated across experimental and nonexperimental subsets and follow-ups, yet the pooled estimate mixes designs, clinical populations, intervention targets, symptoms, measures, and comparators.

claims.confounding_note: Symptom improvement, regression to the mean, expectancy, repeated testing, attrition, treatment selection, measurement overlap, and uncontrolled history can inflate pre-post change estimates.

estimate.metric: standardized pre-post or experimental personality trait score change
estimate.notes: Average marked change around d = .37; emotional stability changed most, followed by extraversion; experimental and nonexperimental subsets both showed change.

limitations: The pooled association does not prove that every intervention changes traits, that score change is durable behavioral change, or which treatment component caused it.

boundary_conditions: Trait measure, symptom overlap, intervention, comparator, baseline severity, and follow-up must be specified.
scope.population: Clinical and nonclinical participants represented in 207 psychological intervention studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Average intervention period of approximately 24 weeks plus source-specific follow-up.

claims.statement: Across 207 intervention studies, personality trait measures changed by about d = .37 on average over roughly 24 weeks, with the largest reported changes in emotional stability, but pooled designs included both true experiments and uncontrolled pre-post studies.

confidence.rationale: The review covered nine major events and found some event-trait patterns, while selection, nonrandom exposure, inconsistent timing, appraisal, measurement, and limited replication prevent strong causal conclusions.

claims.confounding_note: Prior traits can influence event selection and reporting; shared causes, anticipation, age trends, cohort, role demands, appraisal, and concurrent events can produce associations.

estimate.notes: Some evidence of event-specific trait change was found, but the overall evidence was characterized as preliminary.

limitations: A life event label does not specify the actual exposure and does not establish that the event caused the observed change.

boundary_conditions: Event occurrence, subjective appraisal, timing, anticipation, adaptation, prior trajectory, and comparison group are distinguished.
scope.population: Adults represented in prospective studies of nine major love and work life events.
scope.temporal_scope: Personality assessment before and after source-specific life events when available.

claims.statement: Prospective studies provide some evidence that major love and work events are associated with personality trait change, but the nature, timing, shape, and trait specificity of these changes remain preliminary.

confidence.rationale: Longitudinal change, intervention-linked score change, and event associations are compatible with transactional accounts, but the full reciprocal within-person process has not been jointly measured and causally identified.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened when repeated independently measured roles, behavior, and consequences do not predict within-person change beyond measurement artifacts and when changing a candidate process does not alter the prespecified later pattern.
limitations: The hypothesis must not be used to reconstruct a deterministic developmental cause from an adult trait score or biography.

boundary_conditions: Earlier traits, actual exposures, behavior, consequences, later traits, and alternative causes are measured separately.
scope.population: Humans followed repeatedly across changing roles, relationships, environments, or interventions.
scope.temporal_scope: Repeated person-context interactions over months to decades.

claims.statement: Personality development may partly emerge from repeated reciprocal transactions among existing dispositions, selected or imposed environments, roles, relationships, behavior, learning, and consequences.
claims.temporal_ordering: Earlier disposition and context precede repeated behavior and consequences, which precede later measurement, while reciprocal selection remains possible.

evidence.design: Meta-analysis of longitudinal within-sample mean-level change across six broad personality trait categories and life stages.

effect.notes: Trait- and age-specific increases and decreases were reported rather than one universal maturation trajectory.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 92 longitudinal samples and trait-specific mean-level patterns by age.
limitations: Historical cohorts and measures, sparse ages for some traits, and observational longitudinal designs limit causal and current-population interpretation.
evidence.population: Participants from 92 longitudinal samples across adolescence, adulthood, middle age, and old age.
evidence.summary: Average personality trait scores changed across the lifespan in trait- and age-specific patterns.

evidence.design: Meta-analysis of reliable individual differences in longitudinal personality trait change across the lifespan.

effect.metric: variance in individual personality trait change
effect.notes: Reliable individual differences were present for all traits and across the lifespan, with the greatest differences in childhood.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 229 studies, N = 230,492, change heterogeneity for all traits, age patterns, intervals, and measurement moderators.
limitations: Meta-analytic change variance remains model- and measure-dependent and does not identify individual causes.
evidence.population: 230,492 participants in 229 longitudinal studies from childhood through old age.
evidence.summary: People differed reliably in how their measured personality traits changed, including during periods of high average stability.

evidence.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of personality trait score change during clinical and nonclinical interventions, combining true experiments and pre-post designs.

effect.notes: Average change approximately d = .37 over 24 weeks; emotional stability changed most, with variation by presenting problem.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 207 studies, average 24-week duration, d = .37, experimental and pre-post designs, domains, populations, and follow-up persistence.
limitations: Combining controlled experiments with uncontrolled pre-post designs prevents interpreting the pooled estimate as one causal treatment effect.
evidence.population: Participants represented in 207 intervention studies, primarily clinical samples.
evidence.summary: Personality trait measures changed during interventions, but pooled causal interpretation is limited by mixed designs and symptom-trait overlap.

evidence.design: Review of prospective longitudinal research on personality trait change around nine major love and work life events.

effect.notes: Some event- and trait-specific evidence with unresolved nature, timing, shape, and replication.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reviewing prospective evidence for nine major love and work events and describing the overall evidence as preliminary.
limitations: Nonrandom events, personality selection, retrospective event reports, anticipation, adaptation, and inconsistent measurement constrain inference.
evidence.population: Adults represented in longitudinal life-event studies.
evidence.summary: Major life events sometimes accompanied trait-score changes, but evidence was too preliminary for deterministic or general causal claims.

evidence.design: Theoretical integration of prospective event research with longitudinal and intervention evidence represented in this pack.
evidence.extraction_locator: Review rationale linking lasting event-related changes in thoughts, feelings, and behavior to candidate trait change, interpreted with intervention and longitudinal meta-analytic constraints.
limitations: Compatibility across separate literatures is not direct evidence for temporal links in one within-person causal network.
evidence.population: Humans represented in personality development, life-event, and intervention studies.
evidence.summary: Existing evidence is compatible with repeated person-environment transactions but does not identify the complete reciprocal mechanism.

metadata.description: Separates trait constructs, repeated scores, rank-order continuity, mean-level change, individual change differences, life events, interventions, later scores, behavior, and proposed person-environment transactions.
metadata.title: Evidence pack for personality development and change

boundary_notes: Personality development is not one score, one life story, one age trend, or one causal process.
Mean-level change, rank-order continuity, individual differences in change, and measurement change answer different questions.
A trait description is not a diagnosis, moral evaluation, fixed identity, or direct mechanism.
objects.definition: Continuity and change over time in relatively enduring individual differences in characteristic patterns of thought, feeling, motivation, and behavior, represented through declared trait models and measures.
objects.label: Personality trait development

objects.definition: Repeated-measurement context in which comparable personality trait indicators are collected across two or more occasions.

dimensions.comparability: declared trait model, instrument, informant, and invariance evidence

objects.label: Longitudinal personality assessment
objects.scope: Longitudinal personality studies represented in the included meta-analyses.

boundary_notes: Events are not randomly assigned and may be selected by prior personality, circumstances, or both.
objects.definition: Prospective or retrospective assessment context involving a declared transition or event in love, work, health, residence, education, or another life domain.

dimensions.appraisal: occurrence and subjective meaning measured separately when available
dimensions.comparator: nonexposed, differently exposed, or within-person pre-event trajectory
dimensions.timing: before, during, and after when available

objects.label: Major life-event exposure
objects.scope: Prospective personality-change research reviewed by Bleidorn and colleagues.

boundary_notes: An intervention can target symptoms or functioning rather than personality even when trait scores also change.
objects.definition: Study context measuring personality trait scores before, during, or after a clinical or nonclinical intervention.

dimensions.design: randomized experiment, controlled comparison, or pre-post design
dimensions.target: symptoms, behavior, functioning, or personality change

objects.label: Personality intervention assessment
objects.scope: Intervention studies included in Roberts et al. 2017.

objects.definition: Recurring social, occupational, educational, relational, cultural, or material conditions that structure opportunities, expectations, rewards, constraints, and repeated behavior.

dimensions.selection: person may partly choose, evoke, or alter the context

objects.label: Repeated role and environment
objects.scope: Candidate environmental input in transactional accounts of personality development.

objects.definition: Observable action pattern relevant to a declared trait, role, goal, or context and sampled repeatedly across situations or time.
objects.function_note: Behavior can express a trait, adapt to a situation, shape later environments, or reflect skills and states; repeated behavior is not the trait construct itself.
objects.label: Repeated personality-relevant behavior
objects.response_topography: Source-specific social, task, emotional, self-regulatory, exploratory, cooperative, or avoidance behavior.

boundary_notes: Score change can reflect trait change, symptoms, response style, reference group, instrument sensitivity, regression to the mean, or measurement noninvariance.
objects.definition: Score on a declared personality domain or facet collected on comparable occasions from self-report, informant report, or behavioral indicators.
objects.label: Repeated personality trait score
objects.method: Report trait model, instrument, language, informant, scoring, reliability, assessment age, interval, attrition, and longitudinal measurement comparability.

boundary_notes: Average change does not describe every individual and does not preserve rank order by itself.
objects.definition: Statistical estimate of average change in a declared trait score within a sample between measurement occasions.
objects.label: Mean-level personality change estimate
objects.method: Estimate standardized within-sample mean change while reporting age, interval, measure, attrition, cohort, and uncertainty.

boundary_notes: Change variance does not identify why a person changed or whether change was beneficial.
objects.definition: Statistical estimate of between-person variation in longitudinal change in a declared personality trait.
objects.label: Individual differences in personality change
objects.method: Estimate reliable variance in individual slopes or change scores while separating measurement error and reporting age, interval, measure, and sampling assumptions.

objects.definition: Clinical or nonclinical intervention during which declared personality trait measures are repeatedly assessed, whether or not trait change is the primary target.
objects.delivery: Source-specific psychotherapy, psychological treatment, training, or structured intervention compared with a control or preintervention baseline when available.
objects.label: Psychological intervention with personality measurement

boundary_notes: Later score is an observed estimate, not a final identity, developmental endpoint, or proof of the process that produced it.
objects.definition: Declared personality domain or facet score measured after a developmental interval, life event, role exposure, or intervention.
objects.label: Later personality trait score

boundary_notes: Life-event association, age trend, intervention-linked score change, and heritability do not individually identify this complete mechanism.
The process permits stability, change, nonlinear trajectories, different paths to similar scores, and similar experiences producing different changes.
objects.definition: Proposed process in which existing dispositions influence selection, interpretation, evocation, and modification of environments, while repeated roles, relationships, behavior, learning, and consequences contribute to later personality-relevant patterns.
objects.label: Person-environment personality transaction
realization_conditions: Personality, behavior, and environment are measured repeatedly with explicit temporal ordering.
Selection into environments and environmental effects are modeled as potentially reciprocal.
Measurement change is distinguished from durable behavioral and trait change.

sources.authority_note: Lifespan longitudinal meta-analysis used for bounded mean-level change patterns, not individual prediction or causal explanation.
sources.title: Patterns of mean-level change in personality traits across the life course — a meta-analysis of longitudinal studies

sources.authority_note: Recent large meta-analysis used to distinguish reliable individual differences in change from mean-level and rank-order summaries.
sources.title: Individual differences in personality trait changes across the lifespan — a meta-analysis of longitudinal studies

sources.authority_note: Large intervention meta-analysis used with an association claim because the pooled evidence combines experiments and uncontrolled pre-post designs.
sources.title: A systematic review of personality trait change through intervention

sources.authority_note: Prospective life-event review used to show preliminary event associations and constrain deterministic socialization claims.
sources.title: Life events and personality trait change
